title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). K is a number field. T_K = R_{K/Q} G_m. V_K = Ker(N_{K/Q} : T_K -> G_m) is the norm-one torus. V'_K = V_K/R is a quotient torus. E_K is the unit group and E_{1K} the totally positive units (up to finite index). The Proposition states that the following are equivalent:
- (i) the image of the units in V'_K(Q) is finite;
- (ii) V'_K is dominated by a Serre-type torus T_m = T/closure(E_m) for some modulus m;
- (iii) V'_{K,R} is a compact (R-anisotropic) torus;
- (iv) R contains the kernel of V_K -> V_L -> V_L/Im V_{L_0}. Here N_{K/L} is the first map, L is the largest 'Weilien' subfield of K (CM or totally real) and L_0 = L ∩ R. Equivalently, V'_K is a quotient of V_L/V_{L_0}.

This page has three parts.

1. Reduction of (iii). One must determine the compact quotient tori of V_L and show they are exactly the quotients of V_L/V_{L_0}. A deleted sketch notes that V_{L_0} has no compact quotient other than the trivial one.

2. Corollary 1. Let K be Weilien and K_0 = K ∩ R.
- (a) V_K/V_{K_0} is compact.
- (b) V_{K_0} has no nonzero compact quotient torus.
- (c) E_{K_0} has finite index in E_K, i.e. the image of E_K in V_K/V_{K_0} is finite.

Proofs:
- (b): K_0 is totally real, so K_0⊗R ≅ R^r. Hence T_{K_0} and V_{K_0} are R-split, every quotient is split, and a split torus is compact only if trivial.
- (a): trivial if K = K_0. Otherwise K⊗R ≅ C^r and V_K/V_{K_0} ~ T_K/T_{K_0} ≅ [R_{C/R}G_m / G_m]^r ≅ U^r, which is compact.
- (c): Dirichlet's unit theorem gives both K (CM, degree 2r, r_2 = r) and K_0 (totally real, degree r) unit rank r-1.

3. Proof of (iv) ⇒ (i). The norm N_{K/L} sends units to units, and by Corollary 1(c) the units of L are torsion modulo L_0-units in V_L/V_{L_0}.

The next page proves (iii) ⇒ (iv) via character modules. Complex conjugation τ acts as -1 on N/Z (N being the character module of the compact quotient), hence is central in the acting quotient. This forces N ⊂ Z[I_L], i.e. the quotient factors through the maximal CM subfield.

In modern terms, the result is that the largest quotient of the norm torus in which units become torsion is (up to isogeny) R_{L/Q}G_m/R_{L_0/Q}G_m for L the maximal CM subfield. This is the structure of the connected Serre group / infinity types of algebraic Hecke characters of type A_0 (Weil 1955; Serre, Abelian l-adic representations, 1968, ch. II). It is the input for the 'CM part' of the motivic Galois group.
errors: The isomorphism V_K/V_{K_0} ≅ T_K/T_{K_0} is only an isogeny. N_{K/Q} restricted to T_{K_0} is N_{K_0/Q}^2, so the induced map on the G_m quotients is squaring. This is harmless for compactness.
'[K_0:K]=r' should read [K_0:Q]=r (and [K:K_0]=2). The unit ranks r-1 and r-1 are then correct for K CM of degree 2r and K_0 totally real of degree r.
'N_{L/K} applique E_{1K} dans E_{1L}' has the subscript reversed: it should be N_{K/L} : E_{1K} -> E_{1L}.

The step 'compact quotients of V_L are exactly quotients of V_L/V_{L_0}' is only stated on this page. The real argument (τ acting as -1, hence central) is on the next page; the partial deleted argument here is incomplete.

ideas.what: Norm-one torus quotients where global units become torsion are exactly those that are R-anisotropic, and they factor through R_{L/Q}G_m / R_{L_0/Q}G_m with L the maximal CM subfield.
ideas.modern_name: Connected Serre group S^0 / infinity types of algebraic Hecke characters (type A_0) factor through the maximal CM subfield
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (1955) for A_0 Hecke characters; Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968) for the tori S_m, T_m and the CM factorization; Langlands, Deligne, Milne (Serre group) 1970s-80s

ideas.what: Corollary: for K CM, V_K/V_{K_0} is compact (≅ U^r over R), V_{K_0} is R-split, and E_{K_0} has finite index in E_K.
ideas.modern_name: Standard CM-field facts (unit index Q = [E_K : μ_K E_{K_0}] finite; Dirichlet)

ideas.what: The term 'corps weilien' for a field (CM or totally real) whose complex conjugation is central / well-defined on all embeddings.
ideas.modern_name: CM field (or totally real); 'Weil field' in the sense of Weil numbers

missed.claim: In the 1965 motivic Galois notes, Grothendieck independently works out the structure of the Serre torus quotient: units finite ⇔ R-compact ⇔ factors through the maximal CM subfield. This predates or parallels Serre's 1967-68 McGill lectures, and the record does not usually credit it to him. It is however a known result, now standard as the Serre group.
missed.quote: V_{L_0} n'a aucun tore déployé, donc tout quotient est déployé, donc compact seulement s'il est nul. D'autre part V_K/V_{K_0} est compact
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows the Serre group / CM-motive torus was part of Grothendieck's motivic Galois program in 1965. This is relevant to the attribution history of the Taniyama/Serre group as the motivic Galois group of CM motives.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and now standard (Weil, Serre 1968, the Serre group). The only interest is historical: it appears early in Grothendieck's motivic notes, under the term 'weilien'.
transcription_corrections: 'Supposons K [?] [?]' should read 'Supposons K weilien, soit K_0 = K∩R'.
'quotients de T_L V_L' is likely 'quotients de V_L'.

'V_{L_0} n'a aucun tore déployé' should be read as 'V_{L_0} (ou V_{K_0}) étant déployé, tout quotient est déployé...'. Its line begins with K_0 totally real ('Q—R' is probably a garbled 'totalement réel').
'N_{L/K}' (as written in the manuscript) should be N_{K/L}; '[K_0:K]=r' is as written but means [K_0:Q]=r.
'K_R ≃ C^r': the manuscript appears to show C^{r} with a superscript (possibly '3r' misread).
